models: 4 LMs: pre-trained RNN LM (Mikolov et al. 2011), plus 4-gram, RNN and feed-forward LMs trained on Book Corpus
mechanism: Automatic pre-filter dropped passages that any of the 4 LMs found easy, then crowd workers kept passages guessable from the whole passage but not from the last sentence
quote: Any passage whose target word had probability >=0.00175 according to any of the language models was excluded.

mechanism: 95K question-answer pairs written by trivia enthusiasts and scraped from trivia sites; evidence documents added afterwards from Bing search and Wikipedia; no model-based selection

models: IR (retrieval) solver and PMI word co-occurrence solver
mechanism: The Challenge Set keeps only grade-school science questions that both baseline solvers answered incorrectly
quote: The Challenge Set contains only questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based algorithm and a word co-occurence algorithm.

models: IR solver (Clark et al. 2016) and word-association solver (Turney 2017)
mechanism: Crowd-written questions were run through both solvers and edited and retried if either answered correctly; then filtered for human answerability and by an expert
quote: using an automatic filter to ensure hardness for retrieval and association based systems

models: Generator: fine-tuned OpenAI GPT; discriminator: BERT-Large
mechanism: Adversarial Filtering: wrong endings generated by GPT; endings that BERT-Large could easily classify were iteratively replaced; then humans validated
quote: a series of discriminators iteratively select an adversarial set of machine-generated wrong answers

models: RoBERTa (fine-tuned on a small subset, used for embeddings)
mechanism: Crowdsourced twin sentences, then AFLite dropped instances that linear classifiers on RoBERTa embeddings could predict; about 12k debiased items kept from roughly 46k
quote: systematic bias reduction using a novel AfLite algorithm that generalizes human-detectable word associations to machine-detectable embedding associations

models: R1: BERT-Large (SNLI+MNLI); R2: RoBERTa ensemble (+FEVER-NLI, A1); R3: stronger RoBERTa ensemble (+A2)
mechanism: Annotators wrote hypotheses to fool the current model; human-verified model-fooling examples form dev and test
quote: collected via an iterative, adversarial human-and-model-in-the-loop procedure

mechanism: Tasks hand-designed by Chollet in 2019; the semi-private set of 100 tasks was hand-selected in 2024; no model-based selection documented

models: BERT-Large (fine-tuned on 5,000 examples, used for embeddings)
mechanism: Crowdsourced goal and solution pairs, then AFLite discarded instances whose BERT-Large embeddings were predictive of the label
quote: we use AFLite (Sakaguchi et al. 2020) to remove stylistic artifacts and trivial examples from the data

mechanism: Questions collected by hand by graduate and undergraduate students from freely available online sources (exams, textbooks)
Competition problems (AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME and others) taken from AoPS; Level 5 is the hardest AoPS difficulty label

models: GPT-3 175B (seed ideas only)
mechanism: Written by Upwork and Surge AI contractors and re-solved by other workers to check answers; GPT-3 seed questions offered only as inspiration; no solvability filter
Multimodal multiple-choice questions collected from elementary and high school science curricula (IXL); no model-based selection

models: Models evaluated in the BIG-bench paper: GPT-3, Gopher, PaLM, Google internal dense and sparse (BIG-G) models
mechanism: Task-level selection: 23 BIG-Bench tasks where no reported model beat the average human rater; items within tasks sampled at random
quote: a subset of 23 particularly challenging BIG-Bench tasks (27 subtasks) for which no prior result from Srivastava et al. (2022) has outperformed the average human-rater score

mechanism: Written by experts; Diamond keeps questions that expert validators answered correctly and most non-experts (with web access) got wrong; GPT-4 evaluated only as a baseline
369 tasks hand-built by 9 student authors from tutorials, forums and brainstorming, chosen for popularity, helpfulness and diversity; each checked by two humans
quote: The examples are selected by judging their popularity, helpfulness, and diversity, revealed by the views and votes.

mechanism: Original SWE-bench: merged PRs from 12 Python repos, kept if they pass attribute and execution filters. Verified: human developers screened samples and dropped underspecified issues and invalid tests
40 CTF tasks from 4 competitions, chosen to span difficulty by human first solve time
quote: To ensure that the tasks span a wide variety of difficulties, we rely on first solve time.

models: None named; 13 LLMs evaluated at release (o1-preview, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro 002, GPT-4 Turbo, GPT-4o and others)
mechanism: 204 handwritten trick, spatial, temporal and social questions vetted by the team and 4 doctoral reviewers, explicitly designed around weaknesses of current LLMs; no per-item model test documented
quote: The decision to have four types of questions ... was deliberate, to showcase a range of weaknesses of current LLMs.

mechanism: Six existing procedurally generated games (BabyAI, Crafter, TextWorld, Baba Is AI, MiniHack, NetHack) chosen to span difficulty; no item filtering on model success

models: LLMs used only to brainstorm task ideas
mechanism: 175 tasks written by coauthors from O*NET task lists and experience, then checked by hand; no filtering on model performance
All 45 problems from three OTIS Mock AIME exams, written for human contestants and included in full

models: Sonnet, Haiku, o1 Mini, DeepSeek, GPT-4o, Qwen 32B Coder Instruct, GPT-4o Mini (as named in the post)
mechanism: 7 models attempted all 697 Exercism exercises in 6 languages; kept the 225 that 3 or fewer models solved
quote: The new benchmark uses the 225 problems that were solved by 3 or fewer models.

mechanism: Nonstandard ML engineering tasks hand-made by Havard Tveit Ihle; the sources never mention testing tasks on models during design

models: GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, o1; plus o1-mini and o1-preview for text-only questions
mechanism: Before submission, each question was run on the frontier LLMs: exact-match questions had to stump all of them, multiple-choice all but one; then expert review
quote: each question is tested against state-of-the-art LLMs to verify its difficulty ... questions are rejected if LLMs can answer them correctly

mechanism: 100 ball, ramp and bucket diagrams made with a physics simulator by Chase Brower; answers come from the simulation; no model filtering documented

models: LLM judges (grading only)
mechanism: Story briefs with 10 required elements; the same briefs go to every model; graded by a panel of LLM judges; no selection on model scores
Quiz questions on about a dozen long Fiction.live stories, cut to several context lengths; no documented filtering on model results

60+ mathematicians wrote original problems with blind peer review for correctness and guessproofness; models evaluated only after construction (GPT-4o used only in an unpublished check of difficulty ratings)
Street View locations sampled from existing GeoGuessr community maps; no model-based selection

models: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (HCAST QA runs only)
mechanism: HCAST, RE-Bench and SWAA tasks chosen for realism; SWAA written before seeing any AI attempts; agent runs used only to find task bugs
quote: Development of SWAA tasks was blind to AI agent performance; that is, all tasks were written before seeing AI attempts

models: 2020 Kaggle ARC contest entries (brute-force program search); frontier AI reasoning systems such as o3 studied during design
mechanism: Removed eval tasks solved by any 2020 Kaggle entry; new tasks designed around studied weaknesses of AI reasoning systems; every kept task solved by at least 2 humans in 2 or fewer attempts
quote: Removed tasks from eval sets that were susceptible to brute force search (all solved tasks from the original 2020 Kaggle contest).

mechanism: 25 text-to-CAD tasks hand-written by Will Patrick with Fusion 360 reference models; no documented model-based selection

models: Several unnamed LMs with the Terminus 2 agent (QA runs only)
mechanism: Epoch reports Terminal-Bench 2.0: 89 of 229 crowd-sourced tasks, picked by author difficulty estimates and human review; LM runs only checked whether failures were task bugs. TB 1.0 had no documented model filter
quote: we selected 89 for the Terminal-Bench 2.0 dataset based on the author's difficulty assessment and a quality assessment by three experienced human reviewers

models: A few unnamed language models (early candidate validation)
mechanism: Performance commits mined with an LLM judge; some early candidates run on LLMs, and problems where cheap tricks such as memoization matched the human speedup were fixed or removed
quote: we also validated some early candidate problems qualitatively by evaluation on a few language models to identify potential ways in which models can 'hack' problems

models: DeepSeek-V3-0324 (topic classification only)
mechanism: 100 PhD-level tasks proposed by domain experts and screened by hand; an LLM only classified real user queries to set the topic mix

models: o4-mini (May 2025 Symposium); other AI models unspecified
mechanism: About 50 problems, mostly several-week research projects by professors and postdocs; at the May 2025 Symposium about 30 mathematicians were paid per problem o4-mini failed (about 10 succeeded)
quote: Each problem the o4-mini couldn't solve would garner the mathematician who came up with it a $7,500 reward.

models: Original SimpleQA: four GPT-4 models of various dates (later one swapped for GPT-3.5). Verified: GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0 Flash, Claude 3.7 Sonnet
mechanism: Original questions kept only if at least one GPT-4 completion was wrong; Verified kept duplicate-group questions all three models missed and cut to the 1,000 hardest by dropping ones all models solved
quote: we filter the 1,000 most difficult questions from our remaining samples. We do this by again discarding questions which all leading frontier models solve correctly

models: OpenAI models (quality screening only); GPT-4o (occupation classification)
mechanism: 1,320 tasks built from real work products of experienced professionals; model screening flagged only errors, missing files or tasks that looked too small, not model success

models: Unspecified current AI systems (category-level judgment)
mechanism: 240 real freelance projects sourced by Upwork category; Content Writing and similar categories excluded because AIs could already do them; individual projects not filtered
quote: Many projects in the Content Writing category can already be solved by AIs and would not provide much information to include.

models: None (Stockfish engine only)
mechanism: Positions from Stockfish games at random Elo; full-strength Stockfish keeps positions with a single best move the Stockfish player missed; obvious captures dropped; no LLM involvement

models: GPT-5, Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro
mechanism: Banking, consulting and law experts built tasks in simulated work environments, running frontier agents during authoring and iterating adversarially against their outputs
quote: contributors selected from a pool of frontier agents (GPT-5, Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro) to collect outputs, allowing them to adversarially iterate.

mechanism: Vals AI benchmark: problems from qualifying exams and textbooks, formalized in Lean 4 by experts and reviewed; no model testing in selection

models: GPT-5.1 (verifier and no-context ablation only)
mechanism: Tencent Hunyuan and Fudan: experts write contexts containing new knowledge, plus tasks and rubrics, with review rounds; no model-based selection in the full paper
Fixed grid of 4 small base models by 7 existing target benchmarks; agents post-train under a compute budget; no item filtering

models: GPT-5.1 (verifier only)
mechanism: Annotators build real-life contexts (group chats, notes, game logs) and write tasks judged hard by their own judgment; supervisors spot-check; no model testing of drafts
CMU and Bugcrowd (Lee, Brumley): 41 V8 bugs from 2024 or later eligible for v8CTF, graded on 16 capability flags; no model-based inclusion described

models: Frontier agents (verifier QA only)
mechanism: Datacurve: 113 tasks written from scratch; agents run during review only to check verifiers; tasks revised for quality, not solvability

models: Frontier models scored by Cognition (ranking method not stated)
mechanism: Repo maintainers hand-built 150 tasks; Epoch tracks Main, the 100 hardest, and hardness appears to be ranked by model solve rates, excluding the 50 easiest for models
quote: Diamond comprises the 50 hardest tasks, Main the 100 hardest (including Diamond), and Extended the full set of 150.

models: o4-mini (2025 Symposium subset, inherited from v1)
mechanism: Same Tier 4 problems as v1; the June 2026 audit corrected 12 and removed 7 for errors, not because models solved them
quote: Each problem the o4-mini couldn't solve would garner the mathematician who came up with it a $7,500 reward.

mechanism: Same Tiers 1-3 problems as v1; v2 corrected 123 and removed 5 for errors; no removal based on model success reported
16 simulation tasks written by Yann Henon with his own reference solutions; sparse documentation, no model-based selection described

models: Frontier agents (QA only)
mechanism: XLANG: 108 workflows from annotators, practitioner interviews and some LLM-proposed drafts; agent runs used to find rubric gaps and reward hacks; tasks removed only if infeasible or ambiguous

models: AI models (memorization screen only)
mechanism: Epoch and METR: 25 programs chosen by human criteria (compiled, deterministic, testable, feasible for a skilled human); prototype runs informed only size labels
Epoch: one obscure card-based board game (Earthborne Rangers), scored on 21 objectives over repeated playthroughs; no documented model testing in design
Epoch: positions generated by sampling random games of an undisclosed game and keeping mid-game states with a single best move, as in Chess Puzzles; details withheld

models: Unnamed best LLM-based judges
mechanism: Redwood conceptual reasoning set: about half the critiques are LLM-written; some added by active learning, keeping critiques on which the best LLM judges disagreed; items rated by experts
quote: then let some of our best LLM-based judges rate all the critiques, and then added those critiques to the dataset on which the best judges disagree

models: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (wording checks only)
mechanism: Newcomb-like decision theory multiple-choice questions, mostly handwritten by Caspar Oesterheld and checked by a second expert; model answers used only to find unclear wording

models: Frontier models on the v1 leaderboard (not named)
mechanism: Proximal: v1 had 17 expert-curated long-horizon tasks; v2 added 21 and retired 4 v1 tasks, partly because models had saturated them
quote: We retired four v1 tasks that had become saturated or that we were unable to deterministically score

mechanism: Epoch: 60 photos of three IKEA builds chosen by the IKEA Complexity Index, with realistic assembly mistakes made on purpose; no model testing described
